questions.q: What does Rath recommend instead of trying to fix your flaws?
a: Spend your time on what you already do well
Fix every weakness before building any strength
Balance strengths and weaknesses equally
Take a new personality test every year
questions.why: Lesson 1 says we spend too long ironing out wrinkles instead of doubling down on our strengths.

questions.q: How does the summary apply that advice to exercise?
a: Walk daily rather than forcing yourself into the gym
Join a team sport to stay accountable
Lift weights three times a week
Hire a trainer to build discipline
questions.why: Lesson 1 suggests doing the minimum that helps, like a daily walk, and using the rest of your time on strengths.

Someone who plans years ahead with vivid visions
Someone who seeks agreement across a group
Someone who never lets other people down
questions.why: Lesson 2 says a Believer cannot separate motivation from belief and needs a reason to get up.

questions.q: Why does a Futurist make a good co-founder for a Believer?
a: They can give shape to a vision and inspire others to build it
They handle the finances and daily operations
They keep the team calm during conflict
They test every idea against market data
questions.why: Lesson 2 says a Futurist sees past the rules and paints a vivid picture of what the vision could become.

questions.q: What is the main risk for someone with the Responsible strength?
a: Taking on too much and struggling to say no
Avoiding conflict at any cost
Losing sight of the big picture
Growing bored of routine work
questions.why: Lesson 3 says Responsibles try never to let anyone down, so they overcommit and must learn to refuse.
